name: Round Hill Hotel & Villas
positioning: Pastoral, low-rise Jamaican resort west of Montego Bay, opened in 1953, with Ralph Lauren-designed rooms and individually owned villas
best_for: Families who want a villa with its own pool and kitchen, plus a kids' club
Travelers drawn to a resort with a long history of famous guests

facts.text: The resort and its surroundings remain pastoral and low-rise.
Round Hill is about a 20-minute transfer west from Montego Bay's airport.
Jamaican-born entrepreneur John Pringle opened Round Hill in 1953.
The Grill displays framed black-and-white photos of notable past guests, from Paul McCartney to Michael Douglas.
Pineapple House rooms have clean white interiors with navy and pink accents.
Ocean View and Premium Ocean View rooms sit on the upper level, with cathedral ceilings and large windows.
Oceanfront Balcony and Premium Oceanfront Balcony rooms are on the lower level, each with a balcony.
The villas are individually owned and range from two to six bedrooms.
The flagship restaurant, also designed by Ralph Lauren, serves fresh Caribbean food using ingredients from the onsite organic gardens.
The gym is at the spa and offers fitness and yoga classes.
Most of the staff at Round Hill have worked there for over three decades.
There is a kids' club with daily programming, plus water sports rental equipment.

highlights.text: Ralph Lauren, who owns a villa on the property, designed the Pineapple House rooms himself.
John F. Kennedy stayed at Round Hill to write his inaugural speech.
The spa is set in an 18th-century plantation house reached by a path that winds along the beach.
Villas offer shared living spaces, pools, kitchens and outdoor showers.

considerations.text: Montego Bay proper is about a twenty-minute drive away.
The spa is not in the main building; it is reached by a path that winds along the beach.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that reflects the resort's exclusive positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Round Hill Hotel and Villas review
